statement: Assume AC, the full partially one-homogeneous hypotheses, one of the two source boundary alternatives, and the separated bounded-box initialization in the preceding projected-limit theorem. If the Wasserstein gradient flow $\mu_t$ converges in $W_2$ to $\mu_\infty\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R\times\Theta)$, then $\mu_\infty$ is a global minimizer of $F$ over finite nonnegative measures.

Assume AC, the full two-homogeneous hypotheses and separated compact initialization in the preceding global-minimizer theorem. If the Wasserstein gradient flow $\mu_t$ converges in $W_2$ to $\mu_\infty\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, then $\mu_\infty$ is a global minimizer of $F$ over finite nonnegative measures.
relevant_current_facts: **Given:** AC, the assumptions in the Statement, and $W_2(\mu_t,\mu_\infty)\to0$.

statement:
Assume AC. Let $\mu_0,\mu_1\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$. A generalized $W_2$ geodesic from $\mu_0$ to $\mu_1$ with base $
u\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ is a probability measure $\pi$ on triples $(z,x,y)$ whose $(z,x)$ marginal is an optimal coupling of $
u$ and $\mu_0$ and whose $(z,y)$ marginal is an optimal coupling of $
u$ and $\mu_1$; its interpolating curve is $\mu_t=((1-t)x+ty)_\#\pi$. A functional $F$ is $\lambda$-convex along generalized geodesics if for every such $\pi$ its values satisfy $F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1)- rac{\lambda}{2}t(1-t)\int|x-y|^2d\pi$. A vector field $g_\mu\in L^2(\mu;\mathbb R^d)$ is a strong Wasserstein subgradient of $F$ at $\mu$ if for every $\eta\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ and every coupling $\gamma$ of $\mu$ and $\eta$, $F(\eta)\ge F(\mu)+\int g_\mu(x)\cdot(y-x)d\gamma+o\!\left((\int|y-x|^2d\gamma)^{1/2}ight)$ as the coupling action tends to zero, with a remainder uniform over all such couplings. The definition imposes no global displacement-convexity claim.

Assume AC for the flow clause below. Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\rho_X)$ be an input probability space, let $\mathcal H=L^2(\rho_X)$, let $\sigma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and put $\Theta=\mathbb R^{p+1}$ for hidden affine parameters $\theta=(w,b)$. Assume $\phi_\theta(x)=\sigma(w\cdot x+b)$ belongs to $\mathcal H$ for each $\theta$. On $\Omega=\mathbb R\times\Theta$, define the feature map $\Phi(a,w,b)=a\phi_{(w,b)}\in\mathcal H$. For a finite nonnegative Borel measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ for which the Bochner integral exists, its particle-measure predictor is

$$f_\mu=\int_\Omega \Phi(u)\,d\mu(u)\in\mathcal H.$$

The corresponding objective is $F(\mu)=R(f_\mu)+\int_\Omega V\,d\mu$, whenever the scalar integral is finite, with $R:\mathcal H\to[0,\infty)$ a risk functional and $V:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ a regularizer. For the empirical particle law defined on measurable $A\subseteq\Omega$ by $\mu_m(A)=m^{-1}\#\{j:(m a_j,w_j,b_j)\in A\}$, one has $f_{\mu_m}(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\sigma(w_j\cdot x+b_j)$, so a finite one-hidden-layer network is a particle-measure predictor (with an optional constant output bias added separately). A feature-energy Wasserstein gradient flow means an $AC^2_{\rm loc}$ curve of probability measures satisfying the finite-action continuity equation with Borel velocity equal almost everywhere to the negative minimum-norm element of the constrained subdifferential of the first-variation potential. This is the earlier model-flow definition; no existence or uniqueness follows from this definition. The flow use below requires all of the feature-energy regularity hypotheses. In particular, the classical ReLU feature map is not asserted here to meet those hypotheses merely because it is positively homogeneous.

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. For $\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ with finite energy, define $F'(\mu)(u)=dR_{m_\mu}[\Phi(u)]+V(u)$ on $\Omega$, and extend this potential by $+\infty$ off $\Omega$. Its constrained subdifferential at $u$ is the local Fréchet subdifferential of $F'(\mu)+\iota_\Omega$ defined in the feature-measure-energy convention. A Wasserstein gradient flow from $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ is a curve $t\mapsto\mu_t$ in $AC^2_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),W_2))$, with $\mu_{t=0}=\mu_0$, for which there is a Borel velocity $v_t(u)$ satisfying the finite-action continuity equation and $v_t(u)$ equals the negative minimum-norm element of $\partial(F'(\mu_t)+\iota_\Omega)(u)$ for $dt\,d\mu_t(u)$-almost every $(t,u)$. This definition does not assert that the energy is displacement convex.

For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, $\delta_a$ denotes the probability measure concentrated at $a$. For $q>0$, write $\phi_q(z)=(2\pi q)^{-d/2}\exp(-|z|^2/(2q))$.

Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a horizon $T>0$, $0<\epsilon<T$, $a\in\mathbb R^d$, and $c>0$. Take $\mu=\delta_a$ and constant scalar noise $g(t)=c$, so $v(\epsilon)=c^2\epsilon$. Let $\mu_\epsilon$ be the Gaussian-smoothed law with density $\phi_{c^2\epsilon}(x-a)$. For Borel probability laws with finite second moments, define $W_2$ as the square root of the infimum of the quadratic cost over all Borel couplings. Then

$$W_2(\mu_\epsilon,\delta_a)=\sqrt{d}\,c\sqrt{\epsilon}.$$

The coupling bound from the endpoint theorem is therefore an equality in this case.
relevant_current_facts: [F1] For constant $g=c$, the positive-time smoothed law of $\delta_a$ has Gaussian density $\phi_{c^2\epsilon}(x-a)$. [[def-gaussian-smoothed-data-law-and-transition-density]]
[F2] The endpoint coupling estimate is $W_2(\mu_\epsilon,\mu)\le\sqrt{d\,v(\epsilon)}$. [[thm-gaussian-smoothing-endpoint-weak-limit]]
[F3] $W_2^2$ is the infimum of quadratic costs among Borel couplings, and its arguments must have finite second moments. [[def-wasserstein-two-space-and-couplings]]

statement: Assume AC. Let $\Omega=\mathbb R$, $\mathcal H=\mathbb R$, $R(z)=z^2$, $\Phi(x)=\sin x$, and $V(x)=0$, so $F(\mu)=(\int\sin x\,d\mu(x))^2$ for every finite nonnegative Borel measure. For each $r>0$, take $Q_r=[-r,r]$ and $C_1=C_2=1$; the cutoff, boundedness, Lipschitz, and linear-growth assumptions hold. This energy is convex under linear mixtures of measures, but it is not displacement convex along $W_2$ geodesics: along the geodesic from $\delta_0$ to $\delta_\pi$, its endpoint values are zero and its midpoint value is one.
relevant_current_facts: [F2] The unique coupling of two Dirac probability measures is concentrated on their support-point pair, so their $W_2$ geodesic is the linear interpolation of those points. [[def-generalized-wasserstein-geodesic-and-strong-subgradient]]

statement:
Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge1$, take $\mathcal H=\{0\}$, $R=0$, $\Phi=0$, $\Omega=\mathbb R^d$, $V(x)=|x|^2/2$, and $Q_r=\overline B(0,r)$ for every $r>0$. This cutoff family has the required relative-neighborhood property, and $\sup_{Q_r}\|\partial V\|=r\le1+r$, so $C_1=C_2=1$ works. Thus $F(\mu)=\frac12\int|x|^2d\mu(x)$. For any $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, the unique Wasserstein gradient flow is $\mu_t=(e^{-t}\operatorname{id})_\#\mu_0$. The corresponding $m$-particle gradient flow satisfies $x_i(t)=e^{-t}x_i(0)$ under the inner product $m^{-1}\sum_i x_i\cdot y_i$. For every empirical probability $\mu_{m,0}$ and every $t\ge0$,
$$W_2(\mu_{m,t},\mu_t)=e^{-t}W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0),$$
so any initial convergence in $W_2$ persists uniformly on every compact time interval.
relevant_current_facts: **Given:** AC, $d\ge1$, $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, and an empirical initial probability $\mu_{m,0}$.
[F4] Finite-action continuity-equation solutions are represented by absolutely continuous characteristic paths. [[thm-superposition-for-finite-action-continuity-equations]]

statement: Assume AC. In $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, let $\sigma$ be normalized arc-length probability on the unit circle $S^1=\{x:|x|=1\}$ and let $\delta_0$ be the point mass at the origin. For radii $r_a=1/2$ and $r_b=2$, the support of $\sigma$ is contained in the ball $B(0,r_b)$ and separates the two spheres $r_aS^1$ and $r_bS^1$: every continuous path from one sphere to the other meets $S^1$. In contrast, the support of $\delta_0$ is contained in $B(0,r_b)$ but does not separate those spheres. These are only checks of the topological initialization condition; neither example asserts that any flow converges or that its limit is globally minimizing.

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Fix $r>0$ and a nonempty closed convex constraint $D\subseteq\Omega$. For every continuous moment path $m:[0,T]	o\mathcal H$, the nonautonomous inclusion
$$\dot X(t)\in-\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_D)(X(t))-d\Phi_{X(t)}^*
abla R(m(t))$$
has a unique forward solution from each $X(0)\in D\cap Q_r$; its characteristic map is jointly continuous in $(t,X(0))$ and locally Lipschitz in the initial point on each $Q_r$. Let $\mu_t$ and $
u_t$ be two finite-action solutions on $[0,T]$ of the continuity equation with laws concentrated on $D\cap Q_r$ and velocities
$$v_t^\alpha(x)=-\operatorname{argmin}\{|q|:q\in d\Phi_x^*
abla R(m_{\alpha_t})+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_D)(x)\},\qquad\alpha\in\{\mu,
u\},$$
where $m_\alpha=\int\Phi\,d\alpha$. The full shifted minimum selection is Borel; it need not be continuous in position. Each finite-action PDE solution with a continuous prescribed feature moment is the pushforward by its unique characteristic map. For starts in $D\cap Q_r$, these characteristics remain in a larger $Q_R$ uniformly on compact time intervals, and their velocity is the negative full shifted minimum almost everywhere. The same construction applies directly to any continuous forcing $a(t)\in\mathcal H$ in place of $
abla R(m(t))$. Then for all $t\in[0,T]$,
$$W_2(\mu_t,
u_t)\le e^{(C_r-\lambda_V)t}W_2(\mu_0,
u_0),\qquad C_r=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r.$$
Here $A_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|d\Phi\|$, $B_r=\operatorname{Lip}_{Q_r}(d\Phi)$, $M_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|\partial V\|$ in the bounded-selection convention, and $L_r,N_r$ are respectively a Lipschitz constant and a norm bound for $dR$ on the closed convex hull of $\Phi(Q_r)$. In particular, the localized measure-valued flow is unique for each initial law. The estimate does not assume that $v_t$ is continuous in position.
relevant_current_facts: [F1] Each finite-action solution has a path law concentrated on absolutely continuous trajectories satisfying its velocity equation almost everywhere. [[thm-superposition-for-finite-action-continuity-equations]]
[F4] AC supplies the superposition and disintegration constructions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

statement: Assume the feature-energy hypotheses on a closed convex set $Q_r\subseteq\Omega$, and let $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ be concentrated on $Q_r$, with finite feature energy and $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$. Then $F(\mu_n)\to F(\mu)$.
relevant_current_facts: [F2] $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)^2$ is the infimum of $\int|x-y|^2d\pi$ over all Borel couplings $\pi$ of $\mu_n,\mu$. [[def-wasserstein-two-space-and-couplings]]

statement:
Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Fix $r>0$ and let $\mu_0,\mu_1\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ be concentrated on $Q_r$. Let $\pi$ define any generalized $W_2$ geodesic between them, and put $\mu_t=((1-t)x+ty)_\#\pi$. With $C_r=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r$, for every $t\in[0,1]$,
$$F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1)-\frac{\lambda_V-C_r}{2}t(1-t)\int|x-y|^2d\pi.$$
The cost in this inequality is the cost of the specified plan and need not equal $W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ when $\lambda_V-C_r<0$. This does not assert global displacement convexity.

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Fix $r>0$ and $\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ concentrated on $Q_r$. Define $g_\mu(u)=S(\nabla R(\int\Phi\,d\mu),u)$, the minimum-norm element of $d\Phi_u^*\nabla R(\int\Phi\,d\mu)+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(u)$. For every $\eta\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ concentrated on $Q_r$ and every coupling $\gamma$ of $\mu$ and $\eta$,
$$F(\eta)\ge F(\mu)+\int g_\mu(x)\cdot(y-x)d\gamma(x,y)+\frac{\lambda_V-C_r}{2}\int|y-x|^2d\gamma(x,y),\qquad C_r=L_rA_r^2+N_rB_r.$$
In particular, $g_\mu$ is a strong Wasserstein subgradient of the localized functional $F_r$, defined as $F$ on laws concentrated on $Q_r$ and $+\infty$ otherwise, in the all-coupling sense, with zero remainder after the stated quadratic term. Here $A_r=\sup_{Q_r}\|d\Phi\|$, $B_r=\operatorname{Lip}_{Q_r}(d\Phi)$, and $L_r,N_r$ are respectively a Lipschitz constant and norm bound for $dR$ on the closed convex hull of $\Phi(Q_r)$; put $\lambda_r=\lambda_V-C_r$. It is the unique minimum-norm vector field among all all-coupling strong subgradients in $L^2(\mu;\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $r_0>0$ and let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_{r_0}$. Set $M_0=\sup\{\|\nabla R(z)\|:R(z)\le F(\mu_0)\}$, $a=(1+M_0)C_1$, and $b=(1+M_0)C_2$. For $T<\infty$, define
$$r(T)=\begin{cases}(r_0+aT),&b=0,\\(r_0+a/b)e^{bT}-a/b,&b>0.\end{cases}$$
For every $R>r(T)$, the localized flow with indicator $\iota_{Q_R}$ remains in $Q_{r(T)}$ for $0\le t\le T$ and therefore solves the continuity equation with the constraint $\Omega$ alone on this interval. Localized flows with different cutoffs larger than $r(T)$ agree on $[0,T]$. In particular no trajectory starting in $Q_{r_0}$ can escape every cutoff in finite time.

Assume AC, the partially one-homogeneous feature-energy hypotheses on $\Omega=\mathbb R\times\Theta$, and $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\varphi(\theta)$, $V(w,\theta)=|w|\widetilde V(\theta)$ with bounded $C^{1,1}$ feature and penalty maps. In the bounded branch, let $\Theta$ be the closure of a nonempty bounded connected open convex set with $C^1$ boundary and assume $dG_f(\theta)[n_\theta]=0$ for every $f\in\mathcal H$ and $G_f(\theta)=\langle f,\varphi(\theta)\rangle+\widetilde V(\theta)$ and $\theta\in\partial\Theta$. In the unbounded branch, let $\Theta=\mathbb R^{d-1}$ and assume for every $f\in\mathcal H$ that $G_f(r\omega)$ has a uniform $C^1(\mathbb S^{d-2})$ limit as $r\to\infty$, with the dense-regular-value property required by the model. Let $\mu_t$ be the Wasserstein gradient flow from a law whose closed support $K_0$ is contained in $[-r_0,r_0]\times\Theta$ and separates the faces $\{-r_0\}\times\Theta$ and $\{r_0\}\times\Theta$. For every finite $T$, there is $\alpha>r_0$ such that $\operatorname{spt}\mu_t$ is contained in $[-\alpha,\alpha]\times\Theta$ and separates $\{-\alpha\}\times\Theta$ from $\{\alpha\}\times\Theta$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.

Assume AC, the full feature-energy hypotheses on $\Omega=\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and positive two-homogeneity of $\Phi$ and $V$. Let $\mu_t$ be the resulting Wasserstein gradient flow on $[0,T]$. If $K=\operatorname{spt}\mu_0$ is compact, is contained in $B(0,r_b)$, and separates $r_a\mathbb S^{d-1}$ from $r_b\mathbb S^{d-1}$ for $0<r_a<r_b$, then for every $t\in[0,T]$ the support $\operatorname{spt}\mu_t$ separates $r'_a\mathbb S^{d-1}$ from $r'_b\mathbb S^{d-1}$ for some $0<r'_a<r'_b$ depending on the flow and $T$. Here separation means that every continuous path with endpoints on the two spheres intersects the stated support.
relevant_current_facts: [F2] For a continuous moment path the characteristic inclusion has a unique forward solution and a continuous characteristic map; the same supplier states W2 stability for finite-action continuity-equation solutions. [[lem-characteristics-unique-and-stable]]
[F3] A finite-action continuity-equation solution has a path law concentrated on AC trajectories solving its velocity equation. [[thm-superposition-for-finite-action-continuity-equations]]
[A1] AC supplies the Wasserstein flow, superposition representation, and minimum-norm characteristic constructions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

statement:
Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_r$, and let $X:[0,\infty)\to K=L^2(\mu_0;\mathbb R^d)$ be the Hilbert gradient flow of the localized lift $E_r$ from $X(0,s)=s$. Define $\mu_t=(X(t,\cdot))_\#\mu_0$, $m_t=\int\Phi(X(t,s))d\mu_0(s)$, and
$$v_t(u)=-S(\nabla R(m_t),u),$$
where $S(a,u)$ is the minimum-norm element of the full shifted set $d\Phi_u^*a+\partial_{\lambda_V}(V+\iota_{Q_r})(u)$. Then $v$ is Borel, $\int_0^T\int|v_t|^2d\mu_tdt<\infty$ for each $T<\infty$, and $\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0$ in distributions on $(0,T)\times\mathbb R^d$. The curve $\mu_t$ is in $AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),W_2)$, and $v$ is the minimum-action velocity, satisfying $\int_0^T\int|v_t|^2d\mu_tdt=\int_0^T|\dot\mu_t|_{W_2}^2dt$.
relevant_current_facts: [F4] A curve satisfying the finite-action continuity equation is $W_2$-absolutely continuous with squared metric speed bounded by its action. [[thm-continuity-equation-implies-ac2]]

statement: Assume AC. Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ be closed and convex, let $\varphi:\Theta\to\mathcal H$ and $\widetilde V:\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded Lipschitz maps, and set $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\varphi(\theta)$ and $V(w,\theta)=|w|\widetilde V(\theta)$. If $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R\times\Theta)$ and $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$, then $F(\mu_n)\to F(\mu)$.

Assume AC. Let $\Theta$ be either all of $\mathbb R^q$ or the compact closure of a nonempty bounded convex Euclidean domain and let $\phi:\Theta\to H$ and $W:\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded $C^{1,1}$ maps, with $H$ separable Hilbert. Put $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\phi(\theta)$, $V(w,\theta)=|w|W(\theta)$, and assume the feature-energy hypotheses and the prescribed differentiable risk $R\ge0$. Let $\mu_t$ be any flow in the feature-energy Wasserstein definition. Write $m_t=\int w\phi(\theta)d\mu_t$, $f_t=\nabla R(m_t)$, $P_t=\int|w|W(\theta)d\mu_t$, $S(t)=\int w^2d\mu_t$ and $A(t)=\int|v_t|^2d\mu_t$. On every finite interval these quantities have continuous or absolutely continuous representatives as appropriate, and
$$F(\mu_t)-F(\mu_s)=-\int_s^t A(q)dq,\qquad S(t)-S(s)=-2\int_s^t(\langle f_q,m_q\rangle+P_q)dq.$$
These identities hold at every finite pair of endpoints. In particular $F(\mu_t)\le E_0:=F(\mu_0)<\infty$ and $\int_0^\infty A(t)dt\le E_0$. If $\sup_{t\ge0}\|m_t\|\le M$, then, with $D=\sup_{R(z)\le E_0}\|\nabla R(z)\|$,
$$0\le S(t)\le S(0)+2(DM+E_0)t.$$
No bounded-support assumption on the initial weights is required.
relevant_current_facts: [F1] A finite-action continuity-equation solution has a law of absolutely continuous characteristic paths with its time marginals and velocity. [[thm-superposition-for-finite-action-continuity-equations]]

[F1] A finite-action continuity-equation solution has a path law on absolutely continuous curves whose time marginals are $\mu_t$ and whose path derivative is $v_t$ almost everywhere. [[thm-superposition-for-finite-action-continuity-equations]]

statement:
Assume AC and the full feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ be concentrated on a common $Q_{r_0}$, and let $\mu_{m,0}=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\delta_{x_i^{(m)}(0)}$ be empirical laws with every particle in $Q_{r_0}$ and $W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0)\to0$. Define $F_m(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=F(m^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i})$. Here $\partial F_m(x)$ is the Euclidean Fréchet subdifferential: $p\in\partial F_m(x)$ when $F_m(y)\ge F_m(x)+p\cdot(y-x)+o(\|y-x\|)$ as $y\to x$ in $\Omega^m$, with the remainder divided by $\|y-x\|$ tending to zero. A classical particle subgradient flow is a locally absolutely continuous vector $x^{(m)}(t)\in\Omega^m$ satisfying $\dot x^{(m)}(t)\in-m\partial F_m(x^{(m)}(t))$ almost everywhere, under the inner product $m^{-1}\sum_i x_i\cdot y_i$. Let $x_i^{(m)}(t)$ be such flows and put $\mu_{m,t}=m^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i^{(m)}(t)}$. If $\mu_t$ is the unique global measure-valued flow from $\mu_0$, then for every $T<\infty$ there is a finite constant $K_T$ independent of $m$ such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}W_2(\mu_{m,t},\mu_t)\le e^{K_TT}W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0)\longrightarrow0.$$
This is a deterministic continuity estimate in the initial W2 error; it asserts no statistical rate for random initial particles and no conclusion for stochastic gradient descent.
relevant_current_facts: [F4] Localized flows with the same model velocity satisfy the stability estimate $W_2(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le e^{K_Tt}W_2(\mu_0,\nu_0)$. [[lem-characteristics-unique-and-stable]]

statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $d\ge1$, $T>0$, and a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^d$ supported in $\overline B(0,R)$ for some finite $R\ge0$. Let $g:[0,T]\to(0,\infty)$ be continuously differentiable and satisfy $0<g_{\min}\le g(t)\le g_{\max}<\infty$; set $v(t)=\int_0^t g(r)^2\,dr$. On a complete filtered probability space with the usual conditions, let $X_0$ be measurable at time zero with law $\mu$ and independent of future Brownian increments. Let $W$ be a standard adapted $d$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increment $W_t-W_s$ is independent of $\mathcal F_s$ and has law $N_d(0,(t-s)I_d)$ for $0\le s<t\le T$. Let $X$ be the unique strong solution of $X_t=X_0+\int_0^t g(r)\,dW_r$, and write $\mu_t=\operatorname{Law}(X_t)$. For Borel probability laws $\alpha,\beta$ with finite second moments, write $W_2(\alpha,\beta)$ for the square root of the infimum of $\int|x-y|^2\,d\pi(x,y)$ over Borel probability couplings $\pi$ of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. For every $0<\epsilon\le T$,

$$\mathbb E|X_\epsilon-X_0|^2=d\,v(\epsilon),\qquad W_2(\mu_\epsilon,\mu)\le\sqrt{d\,v(\epsilon)}.$$

As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $X_\epsilon\to X_0$ in probability and $\mu_\epsilon$ converges weakly to $\mu$, meaning that $\int f\,d\mu_\epsilon\to\int f\,d\mu$ for every bounded continuous real function $f$ on $\mathbb R^d$. This estimate controls endpoint truncation only: it gives no bound for learned-score error or numerical-discretization error, and asserts no density or score regularity at $\epsilon=0$.
relevant_current_facts: [F4] The positive-time law $\mu_t$ has the stated Gaussian-mixture density, and $\mu_0=\mu$. [[def-gaussian-smoothed-data-law-and-transition-density]]
[F7] For laws with finite second moments, $W_2$ is the infimum of quadratic costs over their Borel couplings. [[def-wasserstein-two-space-and-couplings]]

statement:
Assume AC. Fix $d\ge1$, $T>0$, a Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported in $\overline B(0,R)$ for a finite $R$, and $g\in C^1([0,T])$ with $0<g_{\min}\le g(t)\le g_{\max}<\infty$. Let $W$ be standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion with increments independent of the past, let $X_0\sim\mu$ be independent of future Brownian increments, and set
$$X_t=X_0+\int_0^t g(r)dW_r,\qquad v(t)=\int_0^t g(r)^2dr,\qquad p_t(x)=\int\phi_{v(t)}(x-z)\mu(dz)\quad(t>0).$$
For $0<\epsilon<T$, set $Y_u=X_{T-u}$ on $0\le u\le T-\epsilon$. Then there is a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion $B$ in the usual augmentation of the natural reversed filtration such that
$$dY_u=g(T-u)^2\nabla\log p_{T-u}(Y_u)\,du+g(T-u)\,dB_u,\qquad 0\le u<T-\epsilon.$$
The reverse drift is globally Lipschitz in the state on this truncated interval, with constant at most $g_{\max}^2(1/v(\epsilon)+R^2/v(\epsilon)^2)$ when $\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq\overline B(0,R)$, and has linear growth. The endpoint coupling satisfies
$$\mathbb E|Y_{T-\epsilon}-X_0|^2=dv(\epsilon),\qquad W_2(\operatorname{Law}(Y_{T-\epsilon}),\mu)\le\sqrt{dv(\epsilon)},$$
where $W_2$ is the infimum of root mean-square cost over probability couplings with finite second moments. Consequently $Y_{T-\epsilon}=X_\epsilon$ converges to $X_0$ in $L^2$ and its law converges weakly to $\mu$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. No score or density regularity at $t=0$ is asserted.
relevant_current_facts: [F1] On every $[\epsilon,T]$, $p_t$ is positive and smooth and solves $\partial_t p_t=\tfrac12g(t)^2\Delta p_t$; the Gaussian reverse kernels have the Bayes normalization and composition identities. [[thm-gaussian-smoothing-density-and-forward-equation]] [[def-bayes-reversed-gaussian-smoothing-kernels]]

[F5] With $X_0$ compactly supported, $X_\epsilon$ has finite second moment and the coupling $(X_\epsilon,X_0)$ gives $E|X_\epsilon-X_0|^2=dv(\epsilon)$ and $W_2(\operatorname{Law}(X_\epsilon),\mu)\le\sqrt{dv(\epsilon)}$, hence weak convergence. [[thm-gaussian-smoothing-endpoint-weak-limit]]

Assume AC and the full feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_{r_0}$. There is a unique global curve $\mu:[0,\infty)	o\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ in $AC^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $\mu_{t=0}=\mu_0$ that solves the continuity equation with the negative minimum-norm subgradient velocity of the extended potential $F'(\mu_t)+\iota_\Omega$. For every finite $T$, the curve is concentrated on some $Q_{r(T)}$ and satisfies
$$F(\mu_t)-F(\mu_s)=-\int_s^t\int|v_q(u)|^2d\mu_q(u)dq\qquad(0\le s\le t\le T).$$
For any $\mu_0,
u_0$ concentrated on the same $Q_{r_0}$, their flows obey $\sup_{0\le t\le T}W_2(\mu_t,
u_t)\le e^{K_TT}W_2(\mu_0,

statement:
Assume AC and the feature-measure energy hypotheses. Let $r>0$ and let $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\Omega)$ have finite energy and be concentrated on $Q_r$. There is a unique curve $\mu:[0,\infty)\to\mathcal P_2(Q_r)$ in $AC^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ that starts at $\mu_0$, solves the continuity equation with velocity equal almost everywhere to the negative minimum-norm element of $\partial(F'(\mu_t)+\iota_{Q_r})$, and satisfies
$$F(\mu_t)-F(\mu_s)=-\int_s^t\int|v_q(u)|^2d\mu_q(u)dq\qquad(0\le s\le t<\infty).$$
Writing $\lambda_r=\lambda_V-L_rA_r^2-N_rB_r$, it also satisfies the evolution variational inequality
$$\frac12\frac d{dt}W_2^2(\mu_t,\eta)+\frac{\lambda_r}{2}W_2^2(\mu_t,\eta)\le F(\eta)-F(\mu_t)$$
for each fixed $\eta\in\mathcal P_2(Q_r)$ and almost every $t>0$ (with the exceptional null set allowed to depend on $\eta$). Any two such localized flows obey $W_2(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le e^{-\lambda_r t}W_2(\mu_0,\nu_0)$.
relevant_current_facts: [F2] The Hilbert flow pushes forward to a finite-action continuity-equation solution and an $AC^2$ Wasserstein curve with the displayed minimum pointwise velocity. [[lem-localized-lift-generates-continuity-equation]]

[F4] Along a finite-action continuity equation, squared distance to a fixed measure has derivative bounded above by the velocity-pairing with any optimal coupling. [[lem-w2-distance-derivative-under-a-continuity-equation]]

statement:
Assume AC and the feature-energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_t$ be a Wasserstein gradient flow from $\mu_0$ concentrated on a common cutoff $Q_{r_0}$, with $F(\mu_t)\to F^*:=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}F(\lambda)$. For each $m\ge1$, let $\mu_{m,t}$ be a finite-particle gradient flow for the same objective, with $\mu_{m,0}$ concentrated on $Q_{r_0}$ and $W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0)\to0$. Assume that for every fixed $t$, $W_2(\mu_{m,t},\mu_t)\to0$ as $m\to\infty$, with both laws concentrated on a common cutoff for that finite time. Then both iterated limits exist and

$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}F(\mu_{m,t})=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{t\to\infty}F(\mu_{m,t})=F^*.$$

This is qualitative and gives no rate uniform in $m$ or $t$.
relevant_current_facts: [F1] For every fixed $t$, $W_2(\mu_{m,t},\mu_t)\to0$. [[thm-finite-particle-flows-converge-in-w2]]
